reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the clause auto-renews for successive 1-year terms but the only post-Initial-Term exit requires 90 days' notice, which is at the walk-away boundary and outside the preferred 30-day / fallback 60-day window, and there is no express non-renewal right or renewal reminder.

Redline reaches the preferred position: notice shortened to thirty (30) days, an express non-renewal election added at 30 days before the end of the then-current term, and a Kubient reminder 60 days before renewal; renewal term already 12 months so no change needed.
Omission of a price-uplift cap is justified on the record — compensation is a revenue share set in each Exhibit rather than a fixed fee subject to renewal uplift — so the edit is not rule-incomplete.
Comment is accurate, correctly attributed to the playbook, states what changed and why in the required tone, and offers the 60-day fallback.

The advisory 0.707 changed-character ratio reflects the added non-renewal and reminder sentences the rule expressly requires; the substantive edit remains surgical (surrounding termination-for-breach and fee language untouched).

Minor drafting note for the negotiator (not disqualifying): shortening the mutual for-convenience notice from 90 to 30 days also lets Kubient exit on 30 days' notice; a tighter alternative is to leave the for-convenience period intact and rely solely on the new Customer non-renewal election.
